problem:
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[4]{\pi }}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{\sqrt{\pi }}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x=$

*Hint: Change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$*

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Region

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/8ac5fd57665f292d8a013f47aaf20226944315bb1f74695e895dca40332b28c6.png)

Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
The region of integration is shown above.

*Hint: Change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We cannot integrate the given integral because we cannot find a simple antiderivative of the integrand. So, we change the order of integration.

We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le z\le 1}
$$

The region $R$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/30e43d707479d17f45fb74c023d16706ba9308ffc4421cb17a23d7c2ef16fbee.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/4429082d4ab0d6fdef75d79b1db02944f0c53741fb0ccf19d8a4ef46a253698f.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=(x,z),$ is

$$
z=\sqrt{y}\,⟹\,y={z}^{2}
$$

- The left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le {z}^{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/a941e1bfabb21561b622080775c3c5389a86cf4150f1fb28dd692a022f607620.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by $z=\sqrt{1}=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/20e339260b0947f92d8fedfa47e899ed53753e03e30c4b816edec06d092d9a01.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{z}^{2}}{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{{z}^{3}}[{\int }_{0}^{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{{z}^{3}}{[y]}_{0}^{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{2}\,{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{2}\,{e}^{{z}^{3}}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{e}^{{z}^{3}}}{3}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{e-1}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{e-1}{3}[x]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{e-1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
